diagram_math_checks.justification: By the finite-simple-graph definition and item L1/L2, vertices u=(-1,0), x=(0,1), v=(1,0), y=(0,-1) with edges ux,xv,vy,yu,uv form a simple 2-connected graph. Deleting any vertex leaves a connected subgraph. The diamond boundary and horizontal chord meet only at common endpoints; there are four vertices and five edges in each drawing, with degrees 3,2,3,2.

diagram_math_checks.check: Plane map, domains/codomains and edge images
diagram_math_checks.justification: Phi:R^2 -> R^2 is (s,t) -> (s+2t/5+6,t), inverse (S,T) -> (S-2T/5-6,T), both continuous affine maps. It sends u,x,v,y to the exact plotted u′=(5,0),x′=(6.4,1),v′=(7,0),y′=(5.6,-1) and each straight edge onto its primed edge. Thus Phi restricted to X is the h:X -> X′ boundary-data map of step 6.2.

The linear determinant is +1. Counterclockwise neighbor orders at degree-three vertices are (v,x,y) at u and (x,u,y) at v and match their primed orders; the degree-two vertices introduce no incompatible order. Hence the example satisfies statement (d)(i) with the same epsilon=+1 everywhere.

diagram_math_checks.check: All faces, their frontiers and pairing
diagram_math_checks.justification: Using the complement-component convention of item L2 and def-plane-graph-face-and-boundary, the upper/lower bounded faces have cycles uxvu and uvyu and the unbounded face has cycle uxvyu. Phi sends these to the primed regions: beta(F_i)=F_i′ for i=0,1,2. F0 and F0′ labels lie outside their diamonds; F1/F2 and their primes lie strictly in their respective triangles. Choose F1 and F1′ designated. This realizes (d)(ii), including the outer face, exactly as required in steps 6.2 and 7.1.

The native dark standalone view visibly shows all four outer segments, including y-u and y′-u′, and the chord in each drawing. Four filled vertices, five edges, no crossings or omitted closure, and three distinct face labels per drawing. Only the inter-drawing map arrow is directed; graph edges are undirected. The original proof is unchanged and remains independent of the figure.
